# `get_focuser_setting`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read the focuser and autofocus settings.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build established) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xba5b0 (64-bit build); setting names from handler string table |

No parameters are read. The result always carries the 14 setting members from the in-memory settings (valid whether or not the focuser is open), plus position when the position read succeeds. Internally the handler also tries to print the max_step and backlash controls; in the 64-bit build backlash always fails and is never emitted, and per-read failures omit a member and still return code 0. The strict grade is MUTATOR only because those optional reads write diagnostic log state. Units: af_temp_span is degrees Celsius and af_time_span_hour hours since the last autofocus (READ); af_exp_sec seconds is INFERRED from the name; step fields are UI counts (INFERRED). In a capture run, before a light frame through a non-dark filter, autofocus runs for the first enabled trigger that matches, in this order: af_before_capture, af_wheel_change, af_temp_change_on, af_time_change_on; af_merid_flip runs it after an automatic meridian flip; a failed triggered autofocus does not stop the run (READ).

Side effects: Reads settings memory and optionally the focuser; failed reads write diagnostic log state. No open, close or motion.

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_focuser_setting"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read. Omission, null, object, scalar and array all take the same path. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). ## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":27,"method":"get_focuser_setting"}
```

Reply, ok - All values invented:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_focuser_setting","result":{"fine_step":50,"coarse_step":300,"af_exp_sec":1.0,"af_temp_span":3,"af_init_step":100,"af_time_span_hour":2.0,"af_temp_change_on":false,"af_time_change_on":false,"af_wheel_change":true,"af_before_capture":false,"af_merid_flip":true,"af_track_on":false,"af_only_one":false,"af_bin":2,"position":1200},"code":0,"id":27}
```
